posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
A who-ism is a concept or saying that was popularized (if not created) by the show. 

In this case, the concept of an event, outcome, decision, or moment that must ALWAYS happen, and can never be altered or prevented was created on the show, and given the name "Fixed point".  It was then featured in multiple plot lines, and gradually moved into general time travel lexicons.

I asked the question I wanted to ask about the timelines

"Let us say that Legacy/Young Legacy's death occurs at issue 100, where does Iron Legacy appear in the timeline, does he crash in at issue 50 or issue 150?" (numbers don't matter it was basically before or after)

Something is messing with the multiverse and weakening the walls of reality/normal time. Iron Legacy knows this and tries to extend his rule into the core timeline... at a point before they split.

Iron Legacy is defeated/driven off somehow. However the timelines are so changed that it is possible that Legacy/Young Legacy's death might not even happen in the core timeline any more.

This is just a single part of the story being told through Sentinels.
